records.summary: The Banco Central de Reserva de El Salvador's audited 2023 financial statements put the whole of its physical gold with the Bank for International Settlements, which is the only institution the gold note names.
records.detail: Note 4, 'Oro', of the Banco Central de Reserva de El Salvador's 2023 annual financial statements lists the holding under the heading 'Depositos en Oro Fisico' against one institution, the Bank for International Settlements, and adds that the gold deposits are free of lien or pledge. The statements carry an independent auditor's report by PricewaterhouseCoopers, Ltda. de C.V., engagement partner Wilfredo Peralta, dated 28 February 2024. A second PwC-audited El Salvador document opened separately in this round, the 'Estado de los activos que respaldan la reserva de liquidez' at 31 December 2023 (https://transparencia.gob.sv/institutions/bcr/documents/593992/download), carries the same fact in its own Note 7 'Depositos de oro': a single line, 'Bank For International Settlements $90,964,193.72', against physical gold holdings of 44,105.998 troy ounces. The two documents agree with each other and with an earlier round's independent reading of the same note.
records.evidence_note: Both El Salvador documents are served to the WebFetch tool but 404 to curl on this host, with and without a browser user-agent, so no raw PDF text was obtained and the quoted strings above reach me through the fetch tool's reader rather than from a grep of the file. The quote field is therefore left out, per the common brief. The finding rests on two separate documents fetched separately, whose figures and institution name match, and on round 75's note recording the same Note 4 reading at 44,105.998 troy ounces. Both URLs are reopenable through WebFetch.

records.summary: The Centrale Bank van Suriname's own audited 2020 annual accounts state in one sentence that its entire stock of monetary gold sits at the Royal Canadian Mint.
records.detail: In the Centrale Bank van Suriname's Jaarverslag 2020, the note to the balance sheet on reserve assets, section 4.1(c) 'Monetair goud', opens: 'De voorraad ‘Monetair goud’ bevindt zich bij Royal Canadian Mint.' ('The stock of monetary gold is located at the Royal Canadian Mint.') The note then gives the movement for the year: an opening balance of SRD 598,449,842, sales of SRD 74,889,645, a revaluation of SRD 720,511,150 and a closing balance of SRD 1,244,071,347 at 31 December 2020. No second holder and no other location are named anywhere in the accounts. The volume carries the independent auditor's report; the auditor is BDO Assurance N.V., appointed external auditor of the Bank in 2021, and its report on the 2020 accounts withholds an opinion, the pages of the report setting out why. The entity's head-office city is not stated in the document, so it is left null; the name itself states Canada.
records.quote: De voorraad ‘Monetair goud’ bevindt zich bij Royal Canadian Mint.
records.evidence_note: Raw PDF text, obtained by curl with a browser user-agent and read with pdftotext (15,982,877 bytes, 594,239 characters of text), so the quote is copied from the file rather than from a fetch summary. The quoted sentence appears once in the document. The same note heading was looked for in the newer Jaarverslag 2023 on the Bank's own host (https://www.cbvs.sr/images/content/annual-reports/Jaarverslag_2023_Secured.pdf), which returned HTTP 403, so whether the custodian has changed since 2020 is untested.

abroad_undisclosed.document: Bank Al-Maghrib, Rapport annuel 2025, section 3.2.9 'Commentaires sur les postes du bilan', Note 1 'Avoirs et placements en or'
abroad_undisclosed.quote: Ce poste abrite la contrevaleur en dirhams des avoirs en or conservés au Maroc et auprès de dépositaires étrangers
abroad_undisclosed.note: Bank Al-Maghrib's own gold note says the line covers gold kept in Morocco AND with foreign depositaries, plus gold placements made with foreign counterparties ('ainsi que des placements en or effectués avec des contreparties étrangères'), and it names not one depositary, counterparty, institution or city. The holding is given as 711,078 ounces, about 22 tonnes, worth 28,049,899 thousand dirhams at end-2025. The rest of the document was grepped for 'dépositaire', 'Banque d'Angleterre', 'Banque de France', 'BRI' and 'Réserve fédérale': the only hits are the macroeconomic chapters, the Bank's 11.3 million SDR shareholding in the BIS, and the report's acronym glossary, where 'BoE : Banque d'Angleterre (Bank of England)' appears as a dictionary entry and not as a counterparty. So nothing in this document ties a named institution to the metal, and the Albania trap is avoided. Read from raw text: 9,026,188-byte PDF fetched by curl with a browser user-agent, 862,644 characters extracted by pdftotext and grepped in full; the quote is copied from the extract.
abroad_undisclosed.state: abroad and at home, no institution named

abroad_undisclosed.document: Bank of Papua New Guinea, Annual Report 2024, notes to the financial statements, accounting-policy Note 1(k) 'Gold'
abroad_undisclosed.note: PROVISIONAL AND SUMMARISER-MEDIATED — flagged deliberately, do not file as settled. The BPNG host answers HTTP 403 with a ~3.5 KB block page to curl on three different document paths, with a browser user-agent and with Accept/Referer headers added, so no raw PDF text was obtained. Read through WebFetch in two windows, the document's accounting-policy Note 1(k) 'Gold' was reported to read 'Gold reserves placed on deposit with a financial institution are valued at the Kina equivalent' and 'the underlying transaction means that the Bank holds a gold asset which is separately disclosed as gold', and the Statement of Financial Position carries a gold line of K437,470 thousand for 2024 with no note reference. On that reading the Bank's own accounts place its gold on deposit with an institution they decline to name. Two cautions for the curator: the wording says 'on deposit with a financial institution' rather than 'abroad', so it is a near neighbour of this state and not an exact instance of it; and because round 74 caught the fetch summariser inventing characterisations, the wording above is not verified against the file. Filing it here rather than as a blank keeps the finding visible; it needs one raw-text read to settle, by a route that gets past the bankpng.gov.pg 403.
abroad_undisclosed.state: unnamed institution, wording not verified against raw text

blanks.note: KWT: Central Bank of Kuwait, 'Annual Report 2011/2012' (cbk.gov.kw/en/images/annual-reports-2011-2012-10204_v20_tcm10-10204.pdf, 203,190 bytes, downloaded with a browser user-agent and grepped in full) read on gold. The word gold appears three times in the whole document: as the first line of the statement of financial position, and in significant-accounting-policy 2(a) 'Gold', which reads in full 'In accordance with the Amiri Decree of 4 July 1978, gold is valued at KD 12.500 per fine ounce.' That is a valuation rule and nothing else — no custodian, no depository, no vault, no city, no country. There is no separate gold note behind the balance-sheet line. Also grepped for custodian, deposit with, vault, Bank of England, BIS: no hit touches the gold line. The limit of this blank is its vintage: this is the most recent CBK annual report whose text extracts, the FY2018/19 combined report being substantially an image scan (round 69 recorded that), so a later edition could in principle say more.

FJI: Reserve Bank of Fiji Annual Report August 2023–July 2024, tabled and served as a parliamentary paper (parliament.gov.fj/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Reserve-Bank-of-Fiji-Annual-Report-August-2023–July-2024.pdf, 6,241,558 bytes, 342,184 characters of text, grepped in full), including the audited financial statements with notes. Every gold reference was read: accounting-policy Note 2 'Gold' gives only market valuation and the revaluation-reserve treatment; Note 5 'External reserves' carries the gold line inside the reserves table with no custody wording; the asset-revaluation-reserve note and the currency-risk and credit-risk tables carry the gold line without naming a counterparty for it. The whole document was then grepped for custodian, depository, held with, held at, Bank of England, Reserve Bank of Australia, Reserve Bank of New Zealand and BIS: the only custody hits are the Bank's own Central Securities Depository for domestic securities and term deposits held with financial institutions, neither tied to gold. No location and no holder is disclosed.

BIH: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina, 'Financial statements and independent auditor's report for the year ended 31 December 2025', reached from the bank's own Annual Financial Statements archive at https://cbbh.ba/Content/Archive/1134 and downloaded as https://cbbh.ba/content/DownloadAttachment/?id=53adf4d2-d91b-4b40-8cc6-70cad6057928&langTag=en (1,766,864 bytes, 200,130 characters, grepped in full). Note 11 'MONETARY GOLD' was read in full: it gives the quantity, 112,000 fine ounces at both 31 December 2025 and 2024, the price per fine ounce, the fair value (KM 804,614 thousand for 2025) and the year's movement, and it names no custodian, no depository, no bank and no location. The accounting-policy note on monetary gold (fair-value measurement and the fair-value reserve) adds only valuation. The gold-price-risk note sets a maximum quantity for the portfolio and names nobody. The document was grepped for custodian, deposited with, vault, held abroad, Bank of England and Bank for International Settlements: the BIS appears only as the holder of the Bank's 1,060 BIS shares and the payer of its dividend, 'Deposits with foreign banks (central banks, commercial banks and BIS)' is the cash-and-deposits line and not metal, and the only vault references are the Bank's own banknote vaults. This is the Albania trap and it is refused here too.

TJK: no call was spent on Tajikistan, but the curator should look again at what round 69 already read, because the row's rules have changed since. That round read Note 13 'Золото и прочие драгоценные металлы' of the National Bank of Tajikistan's audited consolidated statements at 31 December 2025 line by line, from the NBT's own financial-reports listing at https://nbt.tj/ru/about/finansovye-otchety.php, and recorded verbatim that the note itemises monetary gold by where the metal is: gold bars in the vault, gold in accounts at foreign banks ('Золото на счетах в иностранных банках', 3,854,498 thousand somoni) and gold at foreign refineries ('Золото на иностранных аффинажных заводах', 728,717 thousand), naming no bank and no refinery. Round 69 filed that as a confirmed blank, which was correct under the rules it had. Under this round's rules it is a textbook instance of gold stated to be abroad with no institution named, and the gold-at-foreign-refineries line is physical metal rather than an account. I have not reopened the document, so I am not filing it as a reclassification of someone else's reading; I am flagging that it can be reclassified from round 69's own verbatim quotes without spending a fetch, and that the same note's vault lines are a candidate home-custody record if the curator will accept 'in the vault' in the NBT's own accounts as the NBT's own vault.
